# Word gaps — shared task board

Two sessions work on how Writer draws Word documents against Word's own
prints, on the `office` branch. This file is how they split the work:
**claim a task before starting it, by editing its `Owner` line and pushing
that edit alone first**, so the other session sees it on its next fetch.
Release a claim the same way if you drop it. The rules each fix found go
in `office.md` ("The painter against Word"); this file only says who does
what next and how to check it.

**STRATEGY (the user, 2026-10-29): Windows mode is the focus.** Word for Windows is the reference, and its
prints (test/corpus/docx/word-win) are the only target. From now on:
- Pick work from the Windows-mode scores only (sweep-win.sh / w-series). Do not chase Mac-only gaps, and do not
  ask for new Mac Word labs; Mac-mode items already on the board are parked unless they also miss in Windows mode.
- Still run the pair in BOTH modes on one base. Windows mode must not drop (the cancelling-errors exception still
  applies, with the uncovered error logged). Mac mode is a guard only: a drop of 1 point or less in a document is
  accepted and noted; more than 1 point blocks the landing until it is explained.
- Word for Windows labs go to `windows` (the box's only Word driver). Other sessions build and pair.

**FOCUS (the user, 2026-10-30): the LibreOffice set (test/corpus/docx/lo).** New work comes from the LO set's misses,
scored in Windows mode against its Word for Windows prints (lo/word-win), v2. Finish and land what is already in flight
on the government corpus, but start no new government-only items. Every LO fix must still not drop the official 756
(the Windows-box confirmation runs both sets). lenovo-2 keeps the LO scores and the triage by class; starling-bd routes
the classes.

**BASELINE (the user, 2026-10-29, later): the Windows box's sweep is the official score.** Scores taken on the Mac
or Linux differ (a Windows host found Thai and rtl gaps the others cannot see: zh-6a4fc013 48.5 there vs 90.7 on a Mac).
- The official numbers are Windows mode, swept ON the Windows box (DESKTOP-URK35LH), its native engine, per the pair
  recipe on this board (8d52c101). windows-1 keeps a rolling base sweep of the office tip there and posts its mean and
  lowest list here after each landing.
- Pick work from that list. A Linux or Mac session may develop and pre-pair on its own host, but before landing it
  pushes a wip branch and asks windows-1 for a Windows-box confirmation (candidate vs the rolling base, Windows mode):
  no document may drop there (the cancelling-errors exception still applies, logged).
- PUSH SAFELY TO office (starling-bd, 2026-10-30, after office was deleted for ~4 minutes and one board commit,
  cf6eab7a, was lost by the restore; it is back as 656eebce). Push only `git push origin HEAD:office` (or a checked
  40-hex hash): never a refspec built from a variable that can come out empty (`:refs/heads/office` DELETES the branch),
  never `--force`, never restore a branch to a tip you fetched earlier without first checking what landed since
  (`git log <your-tip>..<every hash others reported>`). If you ever find office missing or rewound, stop and tell
  starling-bd before pushing anything.
- NEVER STOP PROCESSES BY NAME (starling-bd, 2026-10-30). Three sessions share each machine and its user account, so
  `pkill -f sweep`, `pkill -x swift-build` and `pkill -f "swift-build ... apps/OfficeApp"` each killed or could have killed
  other sessions' builds and sweeps (three times on 2026-10-29/30). Stop only your own work: record the PID when you start a
  job (`$!`, or the PID file your script writes) and `kill <pid>`; on Windows `Stop-Process -Id`. If you did kill by name,
  tell every session on that machine at once.
- NO MAC WORD (the user, 2026-10-29): do not sweep or score against Mac Word's prints (test/corpus/docx/word) any more,
  and print nothing on Mac Word. Pairs are Windows mode only; the Mac-mode guard above is withdrawn. Everything below
  that says "both modes" now means Windows mode.

### Recipe: the 756-document pair on the Windows box (DESKTOP-URK35LH) — reference (Claude windows-1, 2026-10-29)
Scripts are in `~/starling-doc-check/` (same user home for every session on the box). Copy them under your own
names before editing; don't edit mine, and don't build in `starling-win-native` (mine).
- **Build (release only).** The debug build fails on this host (MSVC `construct_at`/`error_code` C++ interop after
  the engine moved to bd7be6b10e59); release works. `f39-build.sh TAG`: sets `STARLING_ENGINE_OUT` and
  `FLUTTER_SWIFT_ENGINE_OUT` to `C:\Users\starling\dev\starling-engine\engine\src\out\host_release` (shared engine, not
  rebuilt), runs `powershell -File sdk/tools/build-windows.ps1 -PackagePath apps/OfficeApp -Product OfficeApp
  -Configuration release` in the checkout, then copies `OfficeApp.exe` + `*.resources` from
  `apps/OfficeApp/.build/x86_64-unknown-windows-msvc/release/` to `bin-TAG/`. Change its `cd` to your own checkout.
  ~9 min incremental, ~17 min cold. Check for running compilers first (`tasklist | grep -iE "swift-build|swift-frontend|swiftc"`).
- **ICU.** If your checkout has no `engine` link, also copy `host_release/icudtl.dat` to `bin-TAG/data/icudtl.dat`;
  without it every document fails "convert failed: unreadable".
- **Sweep.** `wo-sweep.sh TAG WORK KEYFILE [windows|mac]`: PATH += host_release; `STARLING_ICU=<host_release>/icudtl.dat`;
  `OFFICE_FONT_SOURCE=bundled`, `OFFICE_WORD_FONTS=$MODE`, `OFFICE_APP=bin-TAG/OfficeApp.exe`; refs
  `test/corpus/docx/word-win` (windows) or `test/corpus/docx/word` (mac). Runs `test/docx-app-render.sh <R>/test/corpus/docx/docs
  <R>/<refs> WORK keys…`, then `DOCX_WORD_REFS=<refs> python -I test/docx-line-match.py WORK > WORK.match`. Set `R=` to your
  checkout and use ABSOLUTE paths (relative ones fail as "unreadable"). Key file: `all756.txt`, names WITH `.docx`.
- **Pair.** Base and candidate from the same commit, both modes; base and candidate sweep in parallel (~55 min per
  mode). See `pair1.sh`. Outputs: `WORK/` (renders), `WORK.log`, `WORK.match`.
- **Compare.** `python -I wn-mean.py NEW.match OLD.match`: zh/poi means, ≥95 and page-equal counts, movers ≥0.05.
- Windows-host scores differ from Mac-hosted Windows mode (e.g. zh-6a4fc013, Thai); pair on one host only.
- **Faster sweep (2026-10-29): `wp-sweep.sh TAG WORK KEYFILE [MODE] [JOBS]`.** Converts JOBS documents at once with
  `xargs -P` and `timeout 300` each, straight to WORK/pdf, skipping docx-app-render.sh's raster page diff (the line
  match never reads it); scores identical to wo-sweep.sh. `wp-fill.sh` renders only what a stopped sweep lacks;
  `match-both.sh WORK` writes WORK.match (v1) and WORK.v2.match (DOCX_LINE_MATCH=v2). 4 jobs a side for a pair.

  marks/mode/grid picture, E is the gs2 family. A and B: the isolated paragraph's width differs from the in-document one; set aside.

  for 。 ， 、 ；. Not a squeeze limit and not a margin: the quotes are Times New Roman Bold, half-width and giving nothing, as in ours.
  The paragraph is firstLine 643 / firstLineChars 200 on a plain "lines" grid (charSpace 0); Word's first line starts at x 117.26
  (= 85.05 + 32.15, 643 twips), ours at 117.05 (200 chars x 16pt = 640 twips, 32.0): 0.15pt more room in every first line, which is
  the 0.1pt "spare". With the stored 643 ours refuses too (single document, F's line then starts 117.2).

  paragraph stores 560 for 200 chars of 14pt; Word's print starts it 27.25 in, i.e. 13.6pt a character, not 14 and not the stored 14.0).
  Word's "character" for firstLineChars is the face's, not the size: 643 stands for 200 chars in 1,207 paragraphs of ~50 documents,
  640 in 11,620 of ~170. To model it, read the unit per (face, size) from Word's prints: a paragraph's first line x - margin, over
  firstLineChars/100. Open.

  (Word's first line minus its next line's x, charunit2.py in wip/lab-census), 105 start where we count them and 37 where the file's

### Faster pairs: feature index, rule trace, subset sweeps (test/tools/) — LANDED (Linux 01F2SWc8 lenovo-3, 2026-10-30, starling-bd's assignment)
While developing a fix, sweep only the documents it can reach (103 documents: 176 s a sweep, against 18-50 min for 756). The full Windows-box
confirmation (windows-1) stays before landing: it is where already-perfect documents catch regressions.
1. SELECT by feature. `test/tools/docx-select.py 'EXPR' [--keyfile F] [--show A,B] [--count] [--canaries]`. EXPR is Python
   over the features of `test/tools/docx-features.py` (one pass over the packages, ~15 s, cached in ~/.cache/starling;
   `--list` names all ~100: mode, grid, kinsoku_off, langs_ea, tables_merged, textboxes, vml, wordart, charts, smartart,
   header_types, hf_page_field, pagebreak_first, pagebreak_first_before, line_exact, lists, ...). Example, T238's rule:
   `docx-select.py 'mode >= 15 and pagebreak_first_before > 0'` -> 51 documents, every one of the 39 its first cut dropped.
2. TRACE by rule. Put `RuleTrace.hit("name")` (sdk, RichText/RuleTrace.swift) on the branch you changed. With
   `OFFICE_RULE_TRACE=<file>` set it appends "document<TAB>name" once per document that reaches it; unset it does nothing, so
   no score can move (checked: cmp on a full sweep, trace off). `OfficeApp --trace-rules doc.docx` lays a document out as a PDF
   would be written, without writing it. `docx-sweep.sh WORK -t -k SUPERSET` runs it over a superset and leaves
   WORK/trace.keys. It is NOT faster than a conversion (measured: same time, the layout is the cost), so trace a feature-
   selected superset (195 mode-15 documents: 206 s), not all 756.
3. SWEEP the subset. `test/tools/docx-sweep.sh WORK [-k KEYFILE] [-c] [-j 4]`: converts those documents (Windows fonts,
   bundled faces), scores v1 -> match.txt and v2 -> match-v2.txt. `-c` adds the canary set (test/corpus/docx/canaries.txt, 54
   small documents, one or two of each of ~35 feature classes: modes, grids, kinsoku, languages, tables, text boxes, VML,
   charts, SmartArt, footers, page breaks, exact lines, lists, embedded fonts ...). Rebuild it with `--make-canaries`.
   A cheap pair = candidate and base each on `-k keys -c`, then compare match-v2.txt as usual.
Windows-box scripts: any sweep script that reads a list of names can take the key files as they are (one key a line; a key
may be a prefix; a tab ends it).
PROOF, T238 (Linux, office aee18a94 + tools): select 'mode >= 15 and pagebreak_first_before > 0' -> 51 documents (all 39 its first
cut dropped). Trace of the 195 mode-15 documents with t238's hit -> 44 reach it. Candidate pair on those + canaries (98 docs,
185 s a sweep): against the old references 38 of the 39 drops show; against the audited references 41 documents rise, none drop.
Trace off changes nothing: a full sweep with the tools in vs a build without: v1 and v2 score files identical, 755/756 PDFs
byte-identical (zh-b8de3ae2's page 9 differs between ANY two runs; a late-decoded picture).

### Line matcher v2 (test/docx-line-match.py, DOCX_LINE_MATCH=v2) — LANDED; v2 official from windows-1's next baseline (user-approved) (Linux 01F2SWc8 lenovo-3, 2026-10-29, starling-bd's assignment)
Opt-in switch; the default (v1) is byte-identical to the old matcher over a 756-doc Windows base. Report v1 alongside for a
while. v2 reads lines from the page's glyphs: whitespace takes no part; a line is the glyphs on one baseline (origins,
within 2.5pt of the first; the reader's lines cut where the baseline jumps, a smaller raised mark kept with its text);
turned text by its own baseline; a line set out in pieces (0.8 em gaps) matches whole or piece by piece. Full base: mean
98.0 -> 98.1, 111 up, 9 down (all <= 1.6, mostly cells 3-8pt off Word's that v1 merged away: zh-8415d258, zh-e51c31a7,

  glyph tested against the clip path's area (how much of the glyph shows), which PyMuPDF's text API does not give.

ROWPITCH/ROWPITCH2: Word's row pitch is the row height plus ONE rule's width (sz/8 pt) for atLeast and auto rows, at table level or cell level, top-only, bottom-only or both alike; the rule is not added to an exact row; a TOP rule moves the first row down by its width, a bottom rule does not. Ours does this already (15.850/16.100/16.350), except the first row with a bottom-only rule (ours shifts it). tdf152298's 16.08 a row (cell-level bottom rule sz 2) is NOT explained by it (the lab says 16.104): open, a 0.02pt row that costs a row per page over 36 rows. ### Per-mark squeeze model — OWNER lenovo-3 (Linux 01F2SWc8, starling-bd's routing 2026-10-30); findings so far
Tools (Lenovo ~/tmp/word/tools): givecensus2.py (every mark in every line that is identical in Word's print and ours: Word's
step vs ours by font, mark, next and previous class; output give-census2.tsv), marksq.py/markhist.py (step histograms by font),
gapcensus.py/spacegap.py (ideograph-digit gaps). macos-ios's tables: wip/lab-census (markgive-all-756.tsv, sqz-results.tsv).
1. FLOORS (Word, step after a mark before an ideograph, lowest seen): SimSun/FangSong/YaHei , 0.50; 標楷體 ，、。；： 0.73-0.75;
   新細明體 ， 0.76, 。 0.83. A mark followed by a mark goes much lower (， 0.32 ... ), a line's last mark never squeezes (1.000).
2. CAPS ARE NOT THE LEVER. Capping a centred mark's give at a quarter em (off a grid, not the last mark) breaks 90 documents
   that match now (zh-457a8d62 100->6): ~/tmp/word/quarter-v2.patch. Making an opening mark inside a line give nothing
   (the census: Word keeps 《 99.3%, 「 99.4%, “ 99.7%, （ 92-96% whole; ours squeezes 14-26%), in the body only, makes 169
   documents lower and 1 higher (mean 98.1 -> 96.2): ~/tmp/word/opener2.patch. Why: Word's CAPACITY includes the openers; it
   fills closers first, so openers rarely end up squeezed. The census measures the distribution of the drawn squeeze, which a
   line break does not depend on. Do not use per-mark census percentages to set a capacity.
3. Lab cap (windows; zh-bdae17c0 p9, one-cell table, 14pt 標楷體 mode 15): Word squeezes only what the line needs, a comma
   gives 2.04 at most there (3.1 when it must), the CJK-digit gaps give 6.1 -> 3.5 (2.55 each); it took "富" at 9.25 over and
   refused at 9.65: 2/3 of 14.04 = 9.36, the mode-15 two-marks rule already in the code (this section's `mm` labs). So the
   threshold fits; the fault is our overrun (8.7 where Word's is about 9.9 at w:right 0): not the gaps (gapcensus, spacegap:
   ours = Word for 標楷體/FangSong, 0.1 em short only for 新細明體 digits), not the commas (14.04 vs 14.0 an advance).
   Open: where the 1.2pt goes.
4. Lab trail (windows; spaces): in a wordWrap=1 paragraph trailing spaces never wrap by count, they hang, and text after them
   wraps only if it does not fit; wordWrap=0 breaks per character (51 a line). So ours (hang) is right, and zh-621d8756's
   word-win p21 (spaces wrapped 51/51) is probably a STALE REFERENCE: reprint asked.
5. Witnesses waiting: zh-72da925e (a closing 」 halved to take 月 on a spreading grid, a leading "，" kept, a kinsoku-0 "（"
   ending a line), zh-27fc8f9d p2 (《 》 whole where ours squeezes 3.8 each), sqz3's line G (Word holds the squeeze back until
   the line has 5-6pt more room). macos-ios's stored-twips indent fix (52db52eb) may be part of what the half cap covers: re-run
   the quarter cap on top of it when it lands.
- **OPEN, Taiwan fonts: a centred mark gives a quarter em, ours half (Linux 01F2SWc8 lenovo-3, 2026-10-30; lab sent to windows).**
  Word's prints, all 756, step after a mid-line mark before an ideograph, lowest seen: 標楷體 (DFKaiShu) ，、。；： 0.73-0.75 em
  (66149 commas, 10751 squeezed), 新細明體 ， 0.76, SimSun/FangSong/YaHei ， 0.50 (macos-ios's per-face tables agree: DFKai

  both to 9.6 and the digit gaps and takes it (30 characters; need 8.7, room 14.0 of 2 marks). Same shape in zh-073c9234 p9,

**Lab f39 (Word for Windows, 2026-10-28, `~/starling-doc-check/lab/f39`: `mk.py`, `run.sh`, `rd.py`, models).**
zh-f39e54b6's whole package, ONE change per variant, each printed alone in a fresh Word (worker, warm-up, quit).
The two paragraphs are NOT the same: p14 says `leftChars -45 left 1026 rightChars -45 right -108 hangingChars
405 hanging 1134`, p15 `left 1023 hangingChars 404 hanging 1131` — same net first line (−108), different parts.
First line of p14 / p15 (control reproduces the reference: p14 ends "，按", p15 "經查"):

| variant (one change) | p14 takes 日? | p15 takes 查? |
|---|---|---|
| o control | no | yes |
| a p14 gets p15's whole `w:ind` | **yes** | yes |
| b p15 gets p14's whole `w:ind` | yes | **no** |
| c p14 twips → 1023/1131, hangingChars 405 kept | no | yes |
| d p14 hangingChars 405 → 404 alone | **yes** | yes |
| e p14 without the *Chars attributes (1026/1134) | no | yes |
| f p15 without the *Chars attributes (1023/1131) | no | yes |
| g p14's 日 → 查 / h p14's 按 → 經 | no / no | yes |

So the switch is the indent pair, not characters, fonts or position (a 1–5-twip table shift changes nothing).
Hanging in characters is Word's whole twips (405 → 1134, 404 → 1131), as ours already rounds. Sweeps, p14
without *Chars: left L, hanging L+108, right −108, L = 1000…1023: takes iff L mod 5 ∈ {3,4} (period exactly 5
twips). Right swept a twip at a time: L≡0,1,2 take from right −109, L≡3,4 take at −108 and refuse at −107.
Hanging−left D = 105/106/107/109 with right −(216−D) (the same exact room): D105 all take, D106 refuse L≡2 only,
D107 refuse L≡1,2, D109 all take. **Rule (fits all 62 p14 prints, `model5.py`):** the line needs exactly
441.0pt (31 ideographs, 4 spaces of 3.5, two commas squeezed to half — a tie); Word sums the room in doubles,
each measure twips ÷ 20 on its own, column − left + hanging − right, and takes the character iff that sum ≥
441.0 — 440.99999999999994 refuses. Rounding the measures to any unit (1/16pt and finer, half-up/floor/ceil)
fits no more than the first sweep; the float sum fits every print. zh-8d6f702e / zh-5be7e156 (one-twip grid
question): not answered by this lab — a character grid's cells are not this tie; left for a grid lab.

**Lab wa4 (Word for Windows, 2026-10-28, `lab/wa4`) — the WordArt stroke lab 7bd18d8e asked for.** windows-1's wa3
(10-25, never reported) put all cases in one document; wa4 is the same cases, ONE per document, each a fresh Word:
WordWithAttachments' package, mode 14, the 187.5×28.5pt `_x0000_t136` textpath ("Мой текст здесь", Arial Black
20pt, gradient fill) between 10pt centred markers; marker-to-marker baseline distance, and against a bare
`v:rect` of the box (`g`, default 0.75pt stroke, 41.52):

| case | distance | vs rect | | case | distance | vs rect |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| no stroke | 40.68 | −0.84 | | 1pt, round joins | 42.96 | +1.44 |
| 0.5pt stroke | 41.52 | 0.00 | | 4pt, round joins | 70.68 | +29.16 |
| 1pt | 42.96 | +1.44 | | 1pt, "ОООО" | 41.52 | 0.00 |
| 2pt | 51.96 | +10.44 | | 1pt, "IIII" | 41.52 | 0.00 |
| 3pt | 60.24 | +18.72 | | no stroke, "ОООО" / "IIII" | 40.68 | −0.84 |
| 4pt | 70.68 | +29.16 | | shadow offset 3pt, no stroke | 42.96 | +1.44 |
| | | | | shadow perspective, no stroke | 42.96 | +1.44 |

Over the unstroked textpath a stroke adds 0.84 / 2.28 / 11.28 / 19.56 / 30.0 at 0.5/1/2/3/4pt — not linear, and
joins change nothing (so not miter spikes); at 1pt the string decides it (+2.28 for the title, +0.84 for
ОООО or IIII). Either shadow alone adds 2.28. Not built here: tabled for the WordArt-extent owner.

`test/run.sh` termd failure under Linux load versus isolated test, inspect
`termd/test-termd.py`, fix bounded timing tolerance while preserving meaningful

instrumented repeat fails5/70, all received frames are delayed EXIT(type12),

runs. No daemon/rendering behavior changes. Evidence on Linux:

## How a fix is checked

The steering number is `test/docx-line-match.py WORK`: the share of
Word's lines our PDF sets on the same page at the same height (±3pt).
x positions are not compared, so a horizontal fix can be right and move
no score. The loop that has worked:

1. `python3 test/docx-line-match.py WORK KEY 8` (or
   `~/starling-word-check/lab/tools/missed.py WORK KEY` on the Mac) names
   the first line that parts from Word.
2. Read that paragraph's XML and its style; read glyph positions off both
   PDFs (PyMuPDF `get_text("rawdict")`, `get_image_info()` for pictures,
   `get_drawings()` for table rules).
3. When the rule is not obvious, build a lab document from the
   document's own package (`lab/tools/mklab2.py SRC OUT BODY`) and print
   it with Word (`osascript test/docx-word-pdf.applescript IN OUT`; Mac
   only). Labs are named in `office.md`.
4. Sweep the whole corpus, compare per document with the previous
   sweep, and keep only changes where nothing goes down (or say why).
   Convert with `OFFICE_WORD_FONTS=mac`. On macOS there is no `timeout`
   command: a sweep loop using it converts nothing.
5. `test/run.sh --office` (or the release Office tests plus the repository
   checks). As of 2026-10-22 all 454 Office tests pass on the Mac; the old
   LineHeightTests failure came from missing font resources under XCTest.
   Keep the bundled-font startup test passing; do not waive that failure.
6. One fix per commit; fetch and rebase on `office` before every push.

On the Windows box the line match reads the PDFs with PyMuPDF (c4a931e5),
and its numbers sit within a point or two of the Mac's once Chinese text
falls back to YaHei (9ecd33ea) — before that every line drawn there was
JhengHei UI and Yu Gothic UI, and the sample scored 59%. Build and run
as in its memory notes: `STARLING_ENGINE_OUT` to link, the engine's
out-dir on `PATH` and `STARLING_ICU` to run.

Owner: none (Windows 01QbbApP measured it, 2026-10-18)

("強化資金規劃運用能力 | 其它 | 提供資金協助…") starts at 698 of 748 and Word

~/starling-doc-check/lab/rw on the Windows box, each the whole document
with row 120 — the 121st w:tr — changed): the row is never parted, and

(v6), w:widowControl 0 in its paragraphs (v2), w:hideMark off (v7), the
long cell made Web style or wordWrap on (W2, W3), the long text in the
Web cell instead (W4), the last cell 4-6 lines with 3 of room (L12-L20;

lines of room and a cell of 7-10 (R4, R5) — Word leaves the room empty
and starts p28 with it. Rows 73, 78 and 92 of the same table, built the
same way (an empty vMerge cell with no w:p, single-paragraph cells, a Web
cell fourth; 78 the last of its merge too), are parted in the Web cell
with 3 to 7 lines of room. Not found: what the parted rows have that 120
lacks. Next to try: row 73's cells pasted into row 120's place, then
halved until it stops parting.
Done, and it changes the question: row 73 is "模性導入…" alone — the
rows that looked parted (73, 78, 92, …) are rows of their own in the
file, cut where its source's pages broke. Word parts NO row of this
table anywhere: every page of Word's print opens at a row's start.
Ours parts rows, so the question is what makes the whole table's rows
unbreakable. Ruled out, table-wide: w:divId off every row (v9), an empty
w:p in paragraph-less cells (v10), outset borders as single (v11). Not
yet: the compat flags (doNotSnapToGridInCell, growAutofit,
doNotUseEastAsianBreakRules…), the repeated header row (tblHeader), the
exact 16pt cell lines, a fresh table built in this package.

footer, not the table. In zh-73534289's package even a fresh one-row table a page
and a half tall (M73c) skips page 1's 33 free lines and parts from page 2; in
zh-eb54d3b0's package the same body parts on page 1. Bisected: its settings (X1,
X2) and styles (X3) change nothing; its section does (X4). Within the section:
no footer (X5) parts; margins of 1984 (X6) part; footer 200 twips up parts;
bottom margin 1100 parts, 980 does not. Within the footer (a framePr paragraph
holding "8-PAGE", w:w=11907 hAnchor=page x=1 y=-2 wrap=around vAnchor=text, then
an empty Footer paragraph): the frame removed parts (X7); the frame without w:w,
page x=1 y=-2, parts; w:w=3000 at page x=1 or centred on the margin, y=-2, does
not; w:w=11907 with y=1 parts. So an explicitly sized footer frame raised above
its anchor, reaching over the bottom margin, stops Word parting rows at the page's
foot. Built as "a footer with any frame over the margin" it cost ~40 zh documents
(100 -> 11-48: their page numbers are auto-sized frames, y=1, centred on the
margin), so the exact trigger (sized frame, its top over the margin by how much)

Its low ones, unclaimed: zh-884c6e3e 47.2 [Windows 01QbbApP 2026-10-23, lab `zq` on Word for Windows (~/starling-doc-check/lab/zq, this document's own package and paragraph, the first-line indent a plain 2em in twips, the right indent stepped 2 twips): the need is measured from each size's own probe (left-aligned, a break after 征: "2." 0.90 em, every full-width character an em, marks at full width). "征" is TAKEN UP TO / REFUSED FROM: 12pt 5.97/6.07 (0.498/0.506 em), 14pt 6.96/7.06 (0.497/0.504), 16pt 7.90/8.00 (0.494/0.500), 18pt 9.01/9.11 (0.500/0.506), 20pt 9.99/10.09 (0.4996/0.505). From 征's own glyph left plus its em instead, about 0.07pt less. At 16pt by marks on the line before 征: 0 marks (。 and ， made ideographs) -> NO squeeze, refused from 0.00 over; 1, 2 or 3 marks -> exactly 7.90/8.00. So on Windows the limit is half an em, not per mark and not more for more marks, and nothing without a mark to give; each sweep has a single flip. Ours (half the character before) matches it. The Mac's 7.30 at 16pt looks like Mac metrics (fake bold, 楷体_GB2312 substitution) in the natural width, not a different rule. Windows is the tiebreak per the user's decision. ### T89. A table floating against the text: its anchor paragraph stands where the table began — DONE (2026-10-17)
Owner: session 01Xgpbk5jLzrCcB28yZBzYHN (Mac, starling-ios worktree)
zh-fb482d33's landscape roster is `w:tblpPr` vertAnchor text, tblpY 430
twips, full width; after it an empty 12pt paragraph, another, and the
section's mark. Ours set the table its offset down and all three under
it, and the last two took a page of their own (7 pages to Word's 6).
Labs `fb` (Word 16, its package): with "Y" in the first empty paragraph
and "X" in the second, Word sets "Y" at the table's place — the
paragraph after a floating table is its anchor, and the table stands
its offset below that paragraph's top — and "X" under the table. Now the
anchor paragraph, where it fits in the offset on the table's page, is
set at the table's start and the text goes on under the table.

fell; all 128 zh documents have Word's page count.

### Note (Mac 011uWpmC, 2026-10-17): `w:wordWrap` off wraps a paragraph's closing spaces
zh-621d8756 pp 21-27 run a line or two short, every page after p21 late:
its forms end paragraphs in long runs of underlined spaces under
`w:wordWrap w:val="0"`. Lab `ws` (Word 16, p21's paragraphs, four
variants: as is / wordWrap on / no underline / both): the underline does
nothing; wordWrap does. On, the closing spaces hang past the margin out
to the page's edge (lines to x 596 on a 595pt page) and only then wrap,
as ours do. Off, they wrap at the margin as characters do, the last
space straddling it (lines end at 498.8-509.1, margin 505.2):
"陈述申辩人：（…）" and 56 spaces is two lines, a paragraph of 102
spaces two. Tried: holding the closing spaces (no-break, a zero-width
break between each) and plain spaces with the breaks — both overran,
the fitter counting the spaces ~8pt wider over a line than Word and no
space allowed to straddle. Not built; lab in the Mac's scratchpad.
The 8pt is the colons: under `compressPunctuation` (and
noPunctuationKerning) Word sets "：" before a space 11.6pt wide at 15pt
with 0.3 spacing (15.6 in ours), so "执法人员：" + 18 spaces + "执法证号："
+ 15 spaces ends at 509.1 (one space straddling the 505.2 margin) where
ours ends 8.4pt further. Both halves — that compression, and closing
spaces that wrap with one straddling — are needed before the wrap can
be built. Released.

them. So Word places the float first and then moves the content
before its anchor on that page out of its way. Ours keeps floats out of
the paragraphs after their anchor only. Needs a second pass over a page
when a wrapping float lands on content set before its anchor.

### Note from the Linux box (2026-10-17, later): fractional line heights, tried whole-corpus
Measured, not built. skparagraph rounds each line's height to a layout
unit (`InternalLineMetrics::height`, `::round`); a switch that keeps the
fraction (patch kept on the Linux box, off by default, not in the
engine) moved six documents, against the tip with b0b5beab:
- up: zh-e061a08e 94.3 -> 99.8 (the PMingLiU page-foot lead: the Mac's
  1332/1024 em now reaches the foot), zh-d35cbbdb 89.7 -> 100,
  zh-232090e0 95.6 -> 100, zh-6d1afa56 +0.2;
- down: zh-1a3c7aa0 99.7 -> 32.2 (92 pages), bug59058 100 -> 75.4,
  delins 75.0 -> 61.7. Mean 92.5 -> 92.1.

Each loss is a fit that rounding happened to win:
- zh-1a3c7aa0 p13: the "5 O,O-二甲基…" row fits under rounding with no
  room at all (row foot and rule 405.9 of 405.9); with the fraction
  the lines above the table are 0.05 taller and the footer 0.05, and it
  goes over. Ours already stood 0.34pt under Word's at the table's
  head: the 22pt title (方正小标宋_GBK -> YaHei, atLeast 25) is 32.43
  under "附件1" where Word's is 32.16.
- bug59058 p38 (13pt Times as Liberation Serif, MinionPro-It as
  Caladea, atLeast 15): the same 34 lines span 578.64 in Word's print,
  578.35 rounded, 578.90 with the fraction; the page then holds a line
  fewer. The mixed lines (Caladea in them) are the ones that differ.
- delins: the balloons stack by their lines (Word's step 10.46, ours
  10.0 — the Windows box's note above); they move 2-4pt and the
  matcher merges them with body lines.

So the fraction is right where the faces' heights are (the three
Chinese gains), and building it means first fixing what rounding
covered: the title line, the stand-in faces' mixed lines, the balloon
step. An engine change on every platform too (a skparagraph patch
under `patches/`, and a way for Office to turn it on).

text maps them to junk (㒘, 㒡), which DejaVu's presentation forms do not
do. Released: the order is the PDF writer's (the engine's), and a face
whose text cannot be copied out is worse than a wider one.

### T119. Legacy-mode line ends (zh-12c4f07a, zh-749cb15a): first, a compatibility ideograph YaHei lacks — DONE (2026-10-18)

Documents: zh-12c4f07a, zh-749cb15a; zh-5b7ae054, zh-8e8d4c40, zh-4adfcce2, zh-7dc3afad and others hold the same.

YaHei, in the documents holding compatibility ideographs outside that set (counts match per document). Ours gives
the character a whole em, and the line's last character goes over. Fix to try: such a character takes 0.697 em.

the boxes at 0.697 leaves 17.6pt, room for "果" and "。" both; Word took neither, which fits only if its line
breaking counts the box a whole em (then 果 is 4.8 over) and only its drawing is narrow. Its next line ("三、…107年□
施政…首長施", 景、 at 13.33) agrees with a whole-em break. But zh-12c4f07a's "委" fits only with the box at 0.697 in
the break (a whole em leaves it 7.75 over against "，"'s 6.5). Lab wanted (Word for Mac, YaHei, U+F909 and U+FA01):
the box in the break — whole em or 0.697 — and whether it differs by character or position.

Lab answer (Mac 01Xgpbk5, 2026-10-18, Word for Mac 16.113.3,
~/starling-word-check/lab/tools/cj): the break counts the box at 0.697 em
too — a justified 標楷體→YaHei paragraph, U+F909 or U+FA01 at character 11
or right before the marker at 21, gives 0.30 em more room than U+5951 or
U+5EA6 there (78 twips at 13pt, 84 at 14pt; both characters, both places).
So zh-ff93733d's "果。" is something else (its line ends the paragraph
with "。").

With the Mac's lab (the break counts the box at 0.697 too), the box rule is right and moves nearly every changed
line of zh-749cb15a onto Word's (p49-52 and p75-78 runs fixed), but two legacy-mode line ends then go the other
way, so it waits (patch kept by starling-office1-df): (1) zh-749cb15a p? "…功能性及專業性國際組織；" — mid-paragraph,
overflowPunct 0: ours squeezes the line's last mark "；" (over 4.57 of its 7.3) to take "織；", Word carries both (its
p91-93 and p104-113 then run a line apart); (2) zh-ff93733d p1 "…調查結果。" — the paragraph's end, overflowPunct
on: "果" fits whole with the boxes at 0.697 (17.6pt spare) and ours hangs "。", Word carries both (and the rest of
the document runs a line apart: 97.0 -> 6.5). Lab asked of the Mac: in legacy mode, does a line's last mark give
anything to take it — squeezed with overflowPunct off, hung with it on — and does it matter that it ends the paragraph?
Line-end lab (Mac 01Xgpbk5, Word for Mac 16.113.3, zh-ff93733d's package,
compressPunctuation, YaHei 14pt justified, ~/starling-word-check/lab/tools/lp):
the indent up to which the line's last ideograph stays, against a control
of 958 twips (an em is 280). LEGACY: "。" ending the paragraph (overflow
on) 679 — carried with it, no hang, no squeeze; "。" mid-paragraph (on)
958 — hangs; "；" mid-paragraph overflowPunct 0 679 — the last mark is NOT
squeezed to take it; on, 958 — hangs. MODE 15: "。" ending the paragraph
958 — hangs; "；" mid overflowPunct 0 819 — squeezed by half. So legacy
mode squeezes no line-end mark and never hangs a paragraph's final one.

Done with the Mac's labs `cj` and `lp` (Word for Mac; no mode and mode 14 alike, mode 15 not): the box is 0.697 em

### T147. zh-db07d44e p22: a display equation wider than its cell breaks over lines — DONE (2026-10-23)
Owner: none (Linux office1 01Ak4ibJ built it)
Documents: zh-db07d44e (54.8 on Linux; p22 on is a page behind).
Known: p22's cell holds "實績值=(實際取得…/預計…×1/3+實際決標量/預計決標量×1/3+實際併聯量/預計併聯量
×1/3)×100%", an `m:oMathPara` (jc left) round one `m:d`; Word sets it over four lines in its cell, broken
at the "+" signs inside the brackets and before "×100%". `WriterMath` lays an equation out once, at read,
as one unbreakable object, and the cell's line runs past its edge.
Plan: RichLayout asks an object hook for the object's size at the width it has (`objectFitter`);
`WriterMath` breaks a display equation too wide for it at its top-level operators, the delimiter's
content among them, and draws the broken form.
Built: `RichLayout.objectFitter`, asked for a picture-less object wider than its line (in a line or a
paragraph alone); `WriterMath.fit` parts a display equation before its operators — the content of one
bracket round what follows opened up — fills lines greedily, each after the first an inch in, 0.3 em
between them, and the painter draws the form whose width the rectangle has. An equation's runs take the
paragraph's size where they state none (its mark's, its style's, Normal's — not 11), and their East
Asian text the run's `w:eastAsia` face at its line height (標楷體: YaHei on the Mac, 15.8pt rows at 12).
p22 now matches Word's four lines. Same-base sweep of 756: zh-db07d44e 54.8 -> 61.9; nothing else
moved. Then p28's cells "…基準分80分，": a cell's automatic spaces either side of the Latin word before what is
taken give (both of "80"'s, 2.2 of 3.0 in Word's print) — 61.9 -> 98.0, nothing else moved.

### T137. Test bundle: ICU's data loaded before any test lays out text — DONE (2026-10-19)
Owner: none (Linux slides session starling-b2, 01JsizVV, built it)
In the OfficeApp test process ICU's data was never loaded, so the line fitter measured every character at zero
width; loading it late does nothing, since the engine sets up its text state on the first layout. XCTest on Linux
has no hook before the first test, but runs its classes by name: `AAATextSetupTests` sorts first and loads it in its
class `setUp` (`TestText.icuLoaded`, from `STARLING_ICU` or `FLUTTER_SWIFT_ENGINE_OUT`), and `DocxTests` does the
same in its own, for a run filtered to it. The T135/T136 fitter tests now run, not skip, in the full suite (438
tests, 0 failures) and in `--filter DocxTests` (138). One test leaned on the zero widths:
`testABareMarksNumberIsItsParagraphStylesSize` compared its bulleted paragraph with twice the plain one, which held
only while the plain one was a single line; it now compares the two first lines (still failing with the number at
the text's 12pt). Any test that lays text out now measures it for real.

- Linux box, 2026-10-16, a lead (engine side): a justified paragraph
  that opens with ideographic spaces draws its first line an em into the
  left margin — zh-1d3d66d3, zh-04f73697, zh-5f2e209d, zh-301f097c p1,
  "　　本會依據行政院…" (Normal (Web), jc both): Word's first space is at
  the margin (42.5), ours at 30.5, the line's end where Word's is. Left
  aligned, ours is right; with "口口" for the spaces, right. Our line
  fitting counts both spaces (traced with STARLING_RICHTEXT_FIT); a word
  joiner or a box of no width ahead of them moved nothing but 0.9pt, so
  it is the engine's justification of a line holding spaces, not its
  leading-space trim. Found: skparagraph's `TextLine::justify` treats
  every whitespace cluster, U+3000 too, as a stretch — each gives up its
  width for the step, and those at a line's start get no step at all, so
  they collapse and the text after them stands at the margin. Word keeps
  U+3000 an em like an ideograph. The fix is a few lines there (count a
  U+3000 cluster as ideographic in both loops). DONE the same day as an
  engine patch (starling-engine 2ff4aa7219a,
  patches/skia-justify-ideographic-space.patch — Skia stays upstream's,
  patched by scripts/apply_engine_patches.sh after a sync): the four
  reports' first lines start at the margin; an engine built without the
  patch still sets them in it. Leading U+0020 spaces in a justified line
  still collapse (zh-e27cd8bf's "    (一)…"), left as they are.

### Page breaks at a page's foot: a break-alone paragraph needs its line; a break before text does not — MEASURED (Windows 01QbbApP, 2026-10-25)
Lab brk (~/starling-doc-check/lab/brk on the Windows box), zh-0aac9d1a whole in Word for Windows. Its page 7 table ends at 766.5 against a 769.9 foot (3.4pt left). Paragraph 45 is <w:br w:type="page"/> alone (16pt 仿宋_GB2312, on a 15.6pt grid), then paragraph 46 is "附件3":
- (A) as is: the break's paragraph goes to page 8, a blank page with its one empty line at the top, and "附件3" opens page 9 (11 pages). Ours keeps it on page 7: 72.2, ours a page short from there.
- (B) paragraphs 45 and 46 merged (the break, then "附件3", in one paragraph): no blank page; "附件3" opens page 8 (10 pages).
- (C) as (A) with paragraph 45 at snapToGrid 0: as (A).
With T178's zh-167ee06c (its paragraph 52, the break then "附件二之一", at 13.4pt left: Word ends page 6 there, and ours spills its empty pre-break line and makes a blank page), the rule is: a paragraph whose first content is a page break followed by text ends the page where it stands, and its empty line before the break needs no room. A paragraph that is a page break alone needs room for its line like any other, and spills to a blank page when there is none. Ours does the opposite in both.
DONE for zh-0aac9d1a (Windows 01QbbApP, next commit): the existing rule that set a break-only paragraph back under its table where less than a quarter of its line was left now does so only under 2.5pt (zh-60c80728's table leaves 1.3 and Word keeps the break; zh-0aac9d1a's leaves 3.4 and Word gives it a page). The break-then-text half (zh-167ee06c) is lenovo-2's 9fde89a6, by another route.

- A line with word spaces weighs them in the share test at 0.44 of themselves (lab t181: predicts 4.32/3.89/5.93/2.56 for Word's 4.41/3.42/6.20/2.74). ### Browser build: check it before pushing office or sdk code (Linux lenovo-2, 2026-10-25)
396ed439 makes the Office app build, link and load in the browser again; it had been broken since about 2026-10-13,
so test/run.sh's "office: native vs browser" step compared against a stale 10-13 stage and checked nothing since.
- **Pre-push, from now on:** `build/web-app.sh OfficeApp --package apps/OfficeApp` must exit 0 (it builds into its own
  `.build-web-OfficeApp`, so it doesn't disturb `.build-shared` or a running sweep). Then `test/office-layout.sh`.
- **wasm32's Int is 32 bits.** A literal past Int32 (0xFFFF_FFFF) won't compile, and `Int(someUInt32)` TRAPS at runtime
  past 2^31. Compare such sentinels on the raw UInt32 field.
- **No legacy Foundation string layer on the link** (the size gate keeps it off): `str.contains("x")`, even with one
  character, `range(of:)` and `replacingOccurrences` resolve to it and fail as `undefined symbol
  ...Foundation...range2of7options...`. Use `containsSubstring`, `rangeOfSubstring`, `replacingAll`. No NSLock either.
- **Finding the call site behind an undefined symbol:** the linker names only the object file. Map it to the function with
  `llvm-objdump -d -r --no-show-raw-insn <obj>.o | awk '/^[0-9a-f]+ <.*>:$/{fn=$2} /R_WASM.*<symbol fragment>/{print fn}'`
  then `swift demangle --simplified` (script: ~/tmp/wz/scan on the Linux box).
- **V8 rejects a wasm function of more than 1000 parameters** ("param count of 1296 exceeds internal limit of 1000"):
  wasm32's outlined copy of a big enum passes its largest payload field by field. EditOp (two RichParagraphStyles inline)
  hit it and is now `indirect`. Another enum or struct holding several RichParagraphStyle/CharStyle values can do the same as
  those grow.
- **DONE (browser text engine, 2026-10-25):** the browser now runs our own skwasm (c436e31f50a fractional line heights,
  1e327d91201 scaleX, 8bc30c5c89a baseline shift; build/web-app.sh refuses a skwasm missing those exports), and
  office-layout.sh is green with no height tolerance: Mac, and Linux once the native side ran a fresh engine (lenovo-2,
  host_release_lenovo2 at 8bc30c5c89a, all 6 patches; welcome, textedit, word-boringcrypto and both saved copies exact;
  round 3's 18.4/18.6 empty lines were its stale 10-18 snapshot). Redeploying the live sites waits on the user. Was:
- **Was open:** with the stage current, office-layout.sh still fails for real. All three documents break every line the same way,
  but line HEIGHTS differ by fractions (welcome: title 45.5 native vs 46.0 web, body 19.3 vs 19.0). CAUSE: 7ee9e843 (10-17)
  keeps Word lines' fractions through starling-engine's patches/skia-fractional-line-heights.patch (ParagraphStyle bit 13);
  the browser runs Google's prebuilt skwasm, which lacks it and rounds. A 10-13 native build gives 46.0/23.0/19.0, as the
  web does today. Platform gap, not a regression; the fix (own skwasm, a height-tolerant gate, or no fractions on the web)
  is the Mac coordinator's call.

### Office comparison report (starling-office-benchmark, 2026-10-25, pinned 30ed1feb) — five tasks, routed by bd at the user's request
Report: ~/dev/starling/starling-office-benchmark/docs/perf/office-comparison (uncommitted): Starling and LibreOffice against fresh
Windows Office PDFs, SSIM. docx 0.897 / 0.825, pptx 0.632 / 0.896, xlsx 0.977 / 0.728. Showcase: test/corpus/docx/feature-showcase
in that checkout (one editable Word file, 17 sections F01-F17, Word's PDFs beside them).
- T199. Windows stack overflow — DONE 5c48c6ed (windows' d43acae4: `-Xlinker /STACK:16777216` in the Windows link; all three
  export, exit 0). Windows-only flag: the Mac and Linux builds are unchanged, so no sweep can see it. lo-tdf93830, lo-smartart-preserve and 63200 (pptx) die on Windows with 0xC00000FD.
  Checked on the Mac (bd): all three render at `ulimit -s 8192` and segfault at 1024. Windows' main thread gets 1 MB and nothing in our
  build raises it. Fix: a bigger stack for OfficeApp on Windows (a /STACK link flag, or the export on a thread with its own stack).
- T200. Showcase crash on Windows — DONE, engine ce449fad36d (starling; pushed --no-verify once, the user's call: Windows'
  format.bat still runs the full upstream format check that format.sh no longer does). Windows DLL rebuilt: the showcase exits 0,
  19 pages, every page identical to before. NOT the stack. The PDF is written whole, then exit faults: CRT teardown
  destroys SkShaper's HarfBuzz face cache before SwiftFontCollectionManager, whose destructor purges it. Fix in the engine
  (font_collection_bridge.cc: the manager is never destroyed), to starling mainline; windows rebuilds the Windows engine. starling-office-rendering-challenge.docx dies with 0xC0000005 (two fresh runs);
  every F section alone exports. On the Mac it converts to Word's 19 pages, even at a 1 MB stack, so it is Windows-only. Not diagnosed.
- T201. Charts — CLAIMED macos-ios (after zh-b8de3ae2): F07 a three-ring doughnut drawn as one ring; F04 a deleted legend entry
  still shown (also xlsx chart-deleted_legend_entry2's "First"); F09 a 3-D surface drawn as an empty gray box; F03 major unit 2
  where Word's is 1; F10 data-table borders darker and legend keys wider than Word's.
  DONE 5c5d43a4 (Mac 01Xgpbk5) for F04, F07, F09, F10: deleted legend entries left out; a doughnut of n series as n rings, the
  first innermost; a data table that states its lines draws them so, with square keys in its text's ems; surface and 3-D
  surface charts as a projected mesh in value bands (legend = the bands). On sheets the table's own size is scaled as every
  stated size (chart-DataTable-MultipleLegendEntries' table stood 6.8pt for Excel's 9). Pair docx w40 -> w42: nothing moved;

### T203. Installed fonts by default, Starling's stand-ins as a setting — DONE 5997dae3 (Linux office1, starling-office1-95, 2026-10-25)
Owner: Linux office1, routed by macos (the user's decision, from the office comparison report, 4610d248). A family the
machine has is drawn in it; otherwise today's mapping. A setting ("Use fonts installed on this computer", default on / "Use
Starling's matching fonts"), kept across launches; bundled only where there is no local list (web). OFFICE_FONT_SOURCE=

names on macOS, `fc-list : family` on Linux; WASI is always bundled. Backstage has an Options page with the two choices,
saved in office-settings.txt (key fonts=installed|bundled); it applies to documents opened afterwards. OFFICE_FONT_SOURCE wins
and the page says so. Drawing sites (sheets, slides, charts, math, PDF markup, ribbon, convert, dumps) all go through
OfficeFonts.drawn. Every test/ harness and corpus script now defaults OFFICE_FONT_SOURCE=bundled. Gate: same-base pairs with
bundled pinned, Windows mode (word-win refs) and Mac mode, 756 docs each: nothing moved (97.281 / 96.802 both sides).

whose PDF came out corrupt (MuPDF: bad xref, "zlib invalid distance", stray content tokens; 13 bytes longer) — the same

(Settings > General > Fonts) are not listed: an app reaches those only with the
com.apple.developer.user-fonts entitlement ("app-usage") and CTFontManagerRequestFonts. A document named in such a
face falls back to Starling's stand-in. Unclaimed.

### zh-0978dee9 cell baselines (local 10024 / bundled 10035 lines on Windows) — KNOWN MODEL GAP, deferred (macos, 2026-10-29); not claimed (office1 + windows, 2026-10-25)
DEFERRED (Linux 01F2SWc8 lenovo-3, 2026-10-29, macos's call; released): the fix is a per-run Word ascent/descent override in
the SkParagraph patch. The engine already takes a line's max ascent + max descent over its runs, which is Word's rule (lab lh,
(7) under the lab results), but each run's box is the stand-in face's split, not Word's (RichResolvedFace.baseline /
naturalHeight). A strut cannot give per-line heights, and zero-width carriers would be stand-ins. Windows mode: 153 stacked
mixed lines in 46 documents; the 13 under 99 have 1-12 each; zh-0978dee9 is 99+. A day plus engine rebuilds on all three
machines: not worth it now.
Not T203's: Word's print is SimSun + Courier New (p45/p127/p128), lines break alike in all three, and local sits 0.1-0.2pt
under bundled (the strut's even leading splits by the drawn face's ascent/descent). The gap both modes share: p127's cells
stand 0.3-0.5pt under Word's, the 10pt SimSun column at x117.9 0.8-0.9 (Word 100.1 / 113.1 / 126.0, bundled 100.9 / 113.9
/ 126.8), and the matcher regroups cells into rows by y. windows' PDFs: ~/starling-doc-check/t346-{local,bundled}/pdf.
Split by windows' labs c2/mix2/mix3 (~/starling-doc-check/lab/): the shared ~0.4 does not reproduce in a one-row table
(first baselines 100.03 for Word's 100.10). The x117.9 column's extra is its Courier New ASCII: in ours each line holding a
Courier character ("工;", "16", "业;", "料,") sits 0.1-0.2 high and the step after it is 0.3-0.4 long (Word 13.0 throughout),
one run or a run per script alike. The paragraph mixes two line heights at one size, so `_strut` finds it not uniform and
gives no strut; the engine then stacks each run's box — the 宋体 stand-in (YaHei, 1.3 em by YaHei's split) leaves ~2.6pt
under the baseline at 10pt, Liberation Mono 3.0 — and the descent wins. Word sets a mixed line as the most any face reaches
above plus the most any reaches below, by Word's own split per face (RichResolvedFace.baseline / naturalHeight), and 宋体's
13.0 keeps >= 3.0 below. Whole fix: per-line height max(t_i * size) + max((natural_i - t_i) * size). Partial: in `_strut`, a
same-size Latin stretch whose Word box fits inside the East Asian face's keeps `uniform`. windows may take the partial.
Partial dropped (windows, 2026-10-26): Word holds the 宋体+Courier lines at 13.0 but gives a line of Courier "16" alone its own
11.1 — a height per line, which one strut per paragraph cannot give (forced, "16" would stand 13.0). Needs per-line heights in
our own line layout: a model change, open for whoever takes line metrics next.
SCOPED (Linux 01F2SWc8, 2026-10-26, for macos; temporary probe, not committed; tip 545f015d+, engine 5357bf0b374): over all 756 documents, paragraphs that mix faces of different line heights, and their lines by kind —
- Windows mode: 5,061 such paragraphs (19,597 lines). Lines held by our one strut to a taller face they don't contain: 8, in 4 documents. Mixed lines in paragraphs given no strut (the engine stacks each face's box, where Word takes the tallest above + the tallest below): 153, in 46 documents. 48 documents in all; 35 of them already at 99+; the 13 under 99 have 1-12 such lines each (zh-7a16a243 12, zh-ae2dd08d 4, zh-7773163d 3, zh-31d580df 3, …). zh-0978dee9 itself is 99+.
- Mac mode: 7,343 paragraphs (25,355 lines). Held short: 345 in 21 documents, nearly all zh-72da925e (163) and zh-86547e97 (71) — line-grid paragraphs, where holding every line to the tallest is Word's rule (zh-64044a1d), so most are probably right as they are. Stacked mixed: 380 in 55 documents (bug59058 180, zh-0978dee9 48). 24 of the 69 under 99.
Verdict: not worth building now. At most a few tenths on a dozen documents a mode, against a model change that touches the engine's line metrics (one strut per paragraph today; per-line heights need an engine hook or a painter per line), _strut/_tallestOnEveryLine, the fitter's line boxes, pagination cuts (_lineBottoms) and caret/selection rects. Revisit if a lab shows the stacked-mixed lines are a whole-paragraph drift somewhere.
Evidence for it (lenovo-2, 2026-10-26, from macOS-doc's Mac-mode triage): zh-8d72961c (Mac 59.6, Windows 100) is this case and nothing else. Its Chinese paragraph on p1 steps 18, 19, 21, 21, 21 in Mac Word's print. The two lines holding long Latin runs ("Merri-bekCityCouncil", "BellStreet…MorelandRoad") are shorter; ours steps 20, 21, 21, 21, 21, so the page drifts 2-6pt low and 19 lines miss (p1 14, p2 5). Text and breaks are Word's. Not claimed.

### A first character its indent puts past its cell or box — MEASURED (Windows 01QbbApP, 2026-10-26), not claimed; with T210
zh-9bcea239 (92.7) p11: the score cells (tcW 389 = 19.45pt, firstLine 632 = 31.6pt, jc center, vAlign center, HTML autospacing)
hold "5", "4", "5", "6"; Word's print draws none of them, ours draws each at x189.3. Lab ovi (Word for Windows, its package, a
fixed table, Times 15pt): with tcW 389 or 800 and firstLine 632 Word DRAWS the first character, at x121.6 past the cell (ours
108.0); with tcW 800 and firstLine 1200 it OMITS it (ours draws it); the rest of a longer text wraps as ours. So Word sets an
overflowing first character at a fixed place past the cell and leaves it out from some indent on — the document's cells (same
width and indent as the lab's drawn case, plus autospacing and its own cell margins) are past that point. Same family as
T210's text-box "A" (lenovo-2). Lab ~/starling-doc-check/lab/ovi.
RULE, lab ovi2 (the document's own score cell, margins 0, firstLine stepped 300-1400): Word draws the first line's content at its
indent, overflowing the cell, while the indent is short of the cell's right edge — 15pt in the 19.45pt cell, "5" at x105.0 — and
leaves that first line's content out from there on — 20pt and up: nothing. The edge is the cell's width less its left margin:
ovi's 31.6pt in a 40pt column at 5.4 margins is drawn, 60pt is not; the document's cell at 108 margins (31.6 >= 19.45-5.4) is not.
Only the first line goes: "5 abc def" loses "5" and wraps "abc" / "def" from line 2. T210's box "A" (24pt indent, 23.5pt box)
fits the same rule. Ours draws the character always, at x98.2 whatever the indent. CLAIMED Windows 01QbbApP (zh-9bcea239 and
  T210's p12 "A", by arrangement with lenovo-2): wip/indent-past-cell 81d9f7bc — in a cell or box such a first line's word is

### T215. No automatic space after Latin-face digits that follow a full-width mark — TRIED, DROPPED (Linux office1, starling-office1-95, 2026-10-26, routed by macos from windows-1's lab tdn)
zh-147bdae0 p64 "討，102年": Word for Windows sets "102" (Times New Roman) after the "，" with no automatic space either side —
"年" 1.8 after "2", where after "的" it is 4.08 / 3.24 and in 標楷體 digits 4.68. The digits' run takes its paragraph style's
w:hint eastAsia, which sets no digit East Asian: the face decides.
Tried as stated (no automatic space after a run of Latin-face digits that directly follows U+3001-303F / FF01-FF0F /
FF1A-FF20 / FF3B-FF40 / FF5B-FF65): zh-147bdae0 94.4 -> 94.7, but same-base pairs, 756 docs, engine 8bc30c5c89a, had 38
lower in Windows mode (zh-ab1ea005 99.9 -> 34.5, zh-7b5b3de2 100 -> 40.4, zh-51af781b 99.7 -> 67.9, zh-875759ff 99.7 ->
76.7, zh-db07d44e 98.6 -> 86.9 and 33 by under 2) and 46 moved in Mac mode (96.899 -> 96.414). So Word does space digits
after a full-width mark in general; tdn's "，102年" stands unspaced for something narrower — its digits' run takes the
paragraph style's w:hint eastAsia, and its autoSpaceDN is on only by a table style over docDefaults' 0. Reverted. A lab
that crosses those two (the hint, and autoSpaceDN from the table style vs. the paragraph) would split it.
Follow-up lab (windows-1): neither the hint nor where autoSpaceDN comes from matters; Times New Roman digits after the
full-width mark are unspaced, Arial or 標楷體 digits spaced. But the corpus says otherwise in general — Word writes its
automatic space into the PDF as a space glyph, and counting those, Times digits after a full-width mark before an
ideograph are spaced after "，" 221 times and unspaced 128, after "〕" 155 / 23, "（" 210 / 77, "、" 136 / 117 (word-win, all
zh-*). zh-7b5b3de2's "〔2014〕20 号" is spaced in Word's print, and the rule took the document 100 -> 40.4. So "，102年" is
unspaced for a reason still unseen (the unspaced cases are likely documents whose autoSpaceDN is off, which ours already
follows; zh-147bdae0's is on only by the table style). Dropped for good unless a lab names the switch.
Cross (windows-1, lab tdn mk3/mk4): outside a table, Times digits after a full-width mark are spaced wherever autoSpaceDN is
on — zh-147bdae0's paragraph alone in zh-7b5b3de2's package, or in its own with autoSpaceDN turned on, sets 2.5 after "2";
ours already does. Only "，102年" in zh-147bdae0's Table Grid cell stays unspaced, its own autoSpaceDN on or not, where the
same table's "2.102年7月29日" is spaced: one cell's case, left.

### zh-cb56e605 p7 (94.4, word-win): measured, not claimed (Linux office1, 2026-10-26, from macos's w15 list) — a lab question
All 8 misses are p7's table, 12.8pt low in Word's print (rule 148.6, ours 135.8). Between the title (exact 29.4) and the
table stands one paragraph holding a lone U+00A0 in a "LinTimes" run (12pt, kern 0; Windows' sig maps it to Ebrima,
`windowsSigFace`), on a 15.6pt `lines` grid. Word's print draws the nbsp in Ebrima at 130.22 — the slot is three pitches
(46.8 from the title's foot at 101.4 to the table's 148.6; centred, Ebrima's 15.96 puts the baseline at 129.8) — where ours
is two (ours draws it in DejaVu, the stand-in lacking U+00A0, at 123.22). Ebrima's own line, 2724/2048 = 1.33 em, is one
grid's worth over two pitches' half: what makes Word's line over 31.2pt is not found (the mark is 12pt Normal: TNR / 宋体).
A lab: the paragraph alone, the nbsp as a space, in Times, without the grid.
Lab tnb (windows-1): it is the face. Ebrima's 12pt line is 15.96 (win 2210 + 514 / 2048), just over the 15.6 pitch, so the
nbsp's line takes two: the run in Ebrima gives 53.04 title-to-rule, the reference's exactly; as is, Word on windows-1's box
sets LinTimes in Calibri (14.65, one pitch) and gives 39.96, ours alike. Not built: this LinTimes entry has altName "DejaVu
Sans" and no Unicode signature (usb 0/0), so `windowsSigFace` does not apply and ours goes by the alternate; the reference
drew it in Ebrima, windows-1's box in Calibri, and zh-b0207333 — the corpus's one other entry like it — prints Calibri. The
face is the reference machine's own fallback for a missing name, which no file rule reproduces from one document.

### T221. zh-72da925e p13+: table cells wrap a character early — DONE 904c1826 (Linux lenovo-2, starling-d6, 2026-10-26, routed by macos)
Its 12pt cells on a linesAndChars grid of 1.0076 (balanceSingleByteDoubleByteWidth) wrapped "(內" / "湖)" and parted numbers from their years, and its tables paginated apart. ### T216. zh-147bdae0 p39: a run of kept table rows goes over with the row after it — DONE -> 95.0 (Linux office1, starling-office1-95, 2026-10-26, routed by macos)

alone at p38's foot; ours filled p38 with two of them (the row code weighed a kept row only against the paragraph after
the table). Rule: such a run goes over where the page cannot hold it and the first row after it, and one page can — a run

run counts by its first line in each cell (all of it where it may not part): taken whole, zh-499adba6's kept heading row went

100 -> 81 otherwise). Same-base pairs, 756 docs, engine 8bc30c5c89a: Windows zh-147bdae0 94.4 -> 95.0, nothing else moved;
Mac nothing moved. Left in zh-147bdae0: p72-p73's list numbers (59), p19/p27 hyphenation (the user's decision), p64's digits.

### Sub-twip line fit on character grids (zh-5be7e156 p2, zh-8d6f702e p38) — MEASURED, released (Windows 01QbbApP, 2026-10-26, routed by macos)
Witnesses: Word takes zh-5be7e156's p2 "冷" 0.011 over half an em (new engine, x0 110.05 against Word's 109.70) and zh-8d6f702e's p38
"情" 0.007 over; zh-d68ac84a's documented "格" is refused at 0.0016. Lab twip2 (Word for Windows, zh-5be7e156's line in its own section,
right indent stepped by one twip; modes 14 and 15): in mode 14 ours leaves a character exactly one twip sooner than Word at charSpace
-842, -1200, -1600 and -3000 and with it at -2000 and -5544 (0 and -400 drop nowhere in the window); mode 15 drops nowhere but at
0 and -2000, where Word drops and ours not. So ours is never looser than Word, never stricter by more than a twip. A 0.02pt allowance
on such grids in mode < 15 brings -842 and -1600 to Word's but costs the documents: zh-5be7e156 769 -> 767, zh-8d6f702e 816 -> 801
(lines elsewhere taken that Word leaves) — reverted. The gap is in how a gridded line's widths sum (a twip either way per line), not
a tolerance; it needs Word's per-character rounding on a grid, which these labs do not pin. Labs ~/starling-doc-check/lab/{twip,twip2}.

### zh-d0a207ac (95.6, word-win): Wingdings 2 checkboxes drawn as "£" — FIXED 67b573fe (Linux lenovo-2, 2026-10-27; drawn as ☐ at the face's 0.89 em; five Mac-mode drops of 0.3-1.4 are text-layer artefacts — Mac Word's PDF names the box "£" — landed so with macos's OK)
CLAIMED Mac 7bd18d8e (2026-10-29): its 13 footer misses (p10-p16) are a linked footer's fit-to-text box. Sections 2-6
have no footerReference and show section 1's VML "— PAGE —" (mso-fit-shape-to-text, wrap none); a section starts on page
10, and ours re-fitted the box there to "— 10 —" (fit widths were inherited within a section only). Word for Windows keeps
page 1's width and wraps "— 10" / "—" from p10. Fix (Windows pages): inherit from the first page showing the same part,
in any section. Locally 372 -> 386/389; pair running.
Its form (p9-p16, two misses a page) writes checkboxes as `<w:sym w:font="Wingdings 2" w:char="00A3"/>`. Word prints a box (text U+F0A3, Wingdings2). Ours reads the character as U+00A3 in a Wingdings 2 run, and with no Wingdings 2 face it falls to the text face and DRAWS "£". Metafile.symbols maps Wingdings, Webdings and Symbol codes to Unicode glyphs for metafiles, but nothing does so for `w:sym` in runs, and it has no Wingdings 2 table (£ ☐, R ☑, S ☒, …). The fix belongs at drawing time, so the reader's w:sym round-trips. Scoring: Word's text keeps the private code U+F0A3, so even a right glyph scores a miss at a line's edge. It's the drawing that matters. Also p9: its "建筑面积" / "工程造价" labels 3pt apart in ours, one line in Word's.

### T229. `w:topLinePunct` on every line, not just the first — DONE (Linux lenovo-2 01BR2wHn, 2026-10-29, macos's Mac-mode round)
zh-1cfb652b (Mac 90.9): its body paragraphs carry `w:topLinePunct` under `characterSpacingControl doNotCompress`. Both
Word prints start a line that opens with "《" or "（" 8pt left of the margin (仿宋_GB2312 16pt: the mark's blank half) and
take one more character: Mac p2/p12/p14/p15, Windows p14/p15 ("《云南省城市市容…第二十三条进", "（构）筑物…周边环").
Ours squeezes only a paragraph's first line, and only under compressPunctuation (`_topLineSqueeze`, zh-2b955411).
Was next: squeeze an opener at any line's start under `w:topLinePunct`, whatever characterSpacingControl says; pair both modes.
DONE: under `w:topLinePunct` a line's opening mark gives its blank half when the line needs it (first line too where
the settings do not compress — Word's p6 "（一）包秩序…乱刻画、" starts 8.5pt left and takes "画、", the short "（一） 高空抛物；"
keeps its indent), and only it gives where nothing else is compressed. Word takes the half from the mark's left, the line
starting left of the margin; the engine can set nothing before a line's first glyph (a space there is given back by
the justifier, a joiner is folded into the mark, which then overlaps the next character), so ours spreads the half over
the line's characters: the same characters per line, lines ending where Word's do, the line's start at the margin.
Same-base pair, validation engine (ICU + both engine vars pinned, bundled fonts), 756 docs: Windows zh-1cfb652b
98.3 -> 99.4, zh-55087b5f 95.6 -> 100, zh-053f8706 99.2 -> 99.5, mean 97.927 -> 97.935; Mac zh-1cfb652b 90.9 -> 91.7,
zh-55087b5f 97.5 -> 100, zh-053f8706 99.2 -> 99.5, mean 97.557 -> 97.562; nothing lower in either. office-layout gate
(native/browser on the validation skwasm, all Word controls incl. the 12 opener controls) passes.
Left in zh-1cfb652b (Mac): the footer page number box ~6pt low on every page — Mac Word's print puts it where Word for
Windows does (788.4 vs 788.1), so fc321def's Windows-only East Asian charset line holds for the Mac too. DONE as a follow-up (Linux lenovo-2): an embedded face with an East Asian
charset (86/88/80/81) takes the 1.3x line in Mac mode as well. Pair on a fresh base (88320dd12): Mac 97.587 -> 97.590,

### T243. zh-8415d258 (96.2 -> 98.0 on the office tip, 11 of 553 lines) against word-win — RELEASED, measured (Mac 7bd18d8e, 2026-10-30, Windows mode)
The 21 misses of baseline #1 are down to 11 on origin/office 9beb8ba2 with no change of mine: Linux office1's 4e1a1a12 (an em space is an em, the
paragraphs' two leading U+2003) took the first lines. What is left, all on p1-p2, is not a break rule but where the glyphs stand:
- the justified line "化工作的指导意见》（国办发〔2019〕54号），结合水利领域" (p1): Word's line is 412.5 natural + 2.9 spread; it stretches the
  automatic space after "54" by 3.9 (7.62 wide) and the ideographs by 0.12 apiece; ours gives every gap 0.33 (the space 4.08), so the glyphs
  stand up to 2pt off (+0.4 after "化" ... -1.7 after the space) and the line is missed. A justified line with an automatic space: Word's share
  to the space is some 30 times a character's. One witness only; "2022 年9 月29 日" (right-aligned) and "16 个一级" (exact fit, space 3.78,
  ideograph gaps 0) show no such stretch. Not built.
- the signature "<46 spaces>水利部办公厅" (right-aligned, 15pt): Word breaks 水利部办|公厅 (46 spaces + 4 ideographs = 405, the fifth 420 > 415.3); ours
  takes "公" 4.7 over (the legacy half-em take, `x + min(lead, w) - width <= before / 2` in the fitter, with nothing on the line to give).
  Tried guarding that clause for a line of ideographs with no mark and no space (RuleTrace t243-ideographs-alone: 163 documents reach it): the
  214-document pair (reached + canaries) moved nothing, zh-8415d258 included, so the signature line takes the take another way; dropped.
  The trace of that line was not isolated (the fit key "水利部办公厅" also names the cover table's cells).
zh-b62c9e11 is already 100 on the current base. zh-cd8987db (98.3): p7 "5.6.2 … 每a≥3次。" — Word ends the line "…每a≥" (breaks after the East Asian ≥, squeezing three marks); ours kept "a≥3" whole. Built: a line may end after a ≥ or ≤ set East Asian (hinted run), before a non-space. 756 pre-pair (Windows mode, v2, wip/t243-ge-break 97aa86b3): zh-cd8987db 98.3 -> 98.6, zh-447f1d5c 99.4 -> 99.5, ONE dip: zh-0060058e 99.9 -> 99.8 (same 1709/1718 lines; its "≤" paragraph on p41: line 1 now agrees with Word, but ours fits 均 on line 2 where Word's justified line, 0.9pt short, cannot — digits of the stand-in FangSong are 8.00 where Word's are 8.04 (10 digits = 0.4pt) — the old lines matched only because the misplaced ≤ cancelled that). ### T248. LibreOffice FRAMES: drop caps (tdf150438, tdf150200) and the frame that drew nothing (tdf147485) — WIP PUSHED wip/lo-dropcap 0ad7be37c, awaiting windows-1 (Linux office1, 2026-10-30) — LANDED lo-dropcap reader (round 8 passed; windows-1: tdf150438 0 -> 100); lo-dropcap3, lo-frame in round 9
Drop caps were not implemented: the cap's own paragraph (framePr dropCap=drop lines=N, an exact line of N lines) was set on a line of its own and the
text under it. Word sets the cap at (N-1) text lines over the cap height + the text's size (53pt for 11pt text, 3 lines), its baseline on the Nth line's, the
first N lines of the paragraph beside it at the cap's advance. Built (reader, Docx.swift _foldDropCaps): the cap becomes an anchored box (wrapSquare) at the
head of the paragraph after it, and that paragraph takes the cap's width as a left indent — but ONLY when its text fits N lines by an estimate (the engine
does not narrow just the first lines beside a box; wrapping text beside a float is not implemented anywhere, lines are pushed below or not at all). Longer
paragraphs (tdf150200: 5-line paragraphs, dash caps) keep the old setting. NEEDED, bigger: line-by-line narrowing beside a left float (also floattable text,
n775899, square-wrapped pictures). Also found: a Word 2010 inline drawing (wp:inline in mc:Choice) whose VML fallback says position:absolute was read as a
floating object (Docx _float took the VML) and drawn one height above its line — tdf147485's logo; now the line's. tdf147485 still scores 0: Word sets the
frame's group 27pt higher (its y 22.8 for frame y 49.8, the page's top margin 27) and 9pt left of ours, and its WordArt glyph lines are 32.
756 pre-pair (Windows mode, v2): nothing moved. LO set (197 printed): tdf150438 0 -> 100, mean 63.79 -> 64.29, nothing lower.

- SPEC (a): ENGINE PER-LINE WIDTH API for text beside floats (Mac 7bd18d8e, 2026-10-30, starling-bd's request; not built — one engine round with lenovo-3's per-run ascent/descent override).
  WHY: beside a LEFT float the layout holds lines in with a box at each narrowed line's start (`_besideBoxes`, T247 steps 1-4), found by relaying the paragraph out until the line starts settle. Beside a RIGHT float there is no equivalent: a trailing box needs the line's end, which is what is being solved for, and JUSTIFIED text must fill the narrowed measure. tdf97090 (justified Russian beside a right table, Word spreads each narrowed line) waits for this; tdf154703 (left-aligned beside a right frame) can use forced line starts meanwhile.
  API SHAPE (starling-engine + the Swift bridge + wasm): per paragraph, `lineIndents: [(left: Double, right: Double)]` in layout px, indexed by LINE (0-based), the last entry repeating for the lines after it (Skia paragraph's `setIndents` is the left half of this; the right half is new). The line breaker takes `available(line) = maxWidth - left[line] - right[line]` for breaking AND for justification; alignment (left/centre/right/justify) works inside [left, maxWidth - right]; a first-line indent stays the paragraph style's (or becomes left[0]). Swift: `TextPainter.lineIndents` (or on TextStyle's paragraph part) set before `layout`, read back by `computeLineMetrics` as each line's `left` so the existing `line.left`/`width` users are right. Zero-length array = today's behaviour.
  THE LAYOUT CODE THAT WOULD GO: `_besideBoxes` and its emission in `_span` (the RichImageSpan box + `inserts.append`), the `lead` box carrying the first line's beside indent, the offset-map entries those boxes add (`_OffsetMap.inserts` for them), and the forced-line-start insertion of the interim (b). What STAYS: the trial layout that finds which lines the float's band reaches (lines' tops against the band), now with `lineIndents` instead of boxes, and `_besideBand`/`_besideOwn`/`_besideSource` (they say how far and over which stretch); the post-pagination page-share pass; the flow's `besideTable` return. The trial still iterates (an indent changes the line count) but needs no offset map.
  ALSO WANTED THEN: right-hand floats, both-side floats (text left AND right of a centred float: two indents per line, which the box approach cannot do either), tight/through wrap (a per-line indent from the float's outline), Word's text around frames. Related deferred engine change: lenovo-3's per-run ascent/descent override.
- INTERIM (b) (Mac 7bd18d8e, starling-bd's order 2026-10-30): beside a RIGHT float, a LEFT-, CENTRE- or RIGHT-aligned paragraph gets forced line starts at the offsets the narrowed layout finds (a layout-time line-break character in the painter's text, never in the document), so its breaks, y and x are Word's; a JUSTIFIED paragraph beside a right float is left as it was until (a).

### SPEC: THE DEFERRED ENGINE ROUND — per-line indents + per-run ascent/descent (Linux lo5, 2026-10-30, starling-bd's request; NOT scheduled, the user decides)
One round in starling-engine (the SkParagraph patch under engine/src/flutter/third_party + the Swift bridge `Sources/FlutterSwiftBridge/Text.swift` + the wasm build), because both items change the same code (line breaking and line metrics) and cost the same engine rebuild on all three machines (about a day, per lenovo-3's estimate of the second).
1. PER-LINE INDENTS (full spec: "SPEC (a)" above, Mac 7bd18d8e). `TextPainter.lineIndents: [(left, right)]` by line, last entry repeating; the breaker uses `maxWidth - left - right` for breaking AND justification; `computeLineMetrics` returns the shifted `left`. Skia's `setIndents` is the left half; the right half is new.
   WITNESSES: tdf97090 (justified text beside a right table; waits for it), tdf154703 (left-aligned beside a right frame), floattable-multi-col, tdf164500, tdf105688; any text around a right or both-sided float, tight/through wrap, and frames. Layout code that goes away: `_besideBoxes` and its offset-map inserts; the interim forced line starts.
2. PER-RUN ASCENT/DESCENT OVERRIDE (lenovo-3's, zh-0978dee9 note above). Each run's box in a line takes the stand-in face's ascent/descent; Word's are the real face's (RichResolvedFace.baseline / naturalHeight). The engine already takes a line's max ascent + max descent over its runs, which is Word's rule (lab lh), so the fix is a `TextStyle` pair `(ascent, descent)` in layout px that replaces the face's for that run's box (and its strut share), nothing else. A strut cannot give per-line heights; zero-width carriers would be stand-ins.
   WITNESSES: 153 stacked mixed-face lines in 46 documents of the 756 (Windows mode): zh-0978dee9 (cells 0.3-0.9pt off), zh-6e7ff836 (rows 0.6pt apart, Latin + 標楷體), the 13 documents under 99 with 1-12 such lines each. Expected gain small per document, many documents.
3. GATES (both): the 756 and the LO set pair on Windows mode with the NEW engine on every machine before any layout change relies on it; the old layout paths stay until a pair shows the new one equal or better (a `lineIndents` empty array and unset ascent/descent are today's behaviour, so the engine change alone must move nothing). Order: engine + bridge first (no layout change, pair = identical), then item 2's layout hook (smaller), then item 1's (removes the box machinery). Build/ABI: bump the bridge symbol set together (`host_debug` AND `host_release` per CLAUDE.md, or the release shell fails at runtime on the first call).
4. COST: the engine change is small (two fields through the paragraph builder); the cost is the three-machine engine rebuilds (about 20 min each plus the wasm), the pairs, and the layout work of item 1 (the trial relayout stays, minus the offset map).

### Linux lo5 — fdo77887 / fdo48718-1: the cut of a FLOATING outer row (labs nt1, nt1b by windows, 2026-10-30)

CAUSE (measured, not a guess). The attendance table is a 76-row table nested in the one cell of a one-row OUTER table that is itself a floating table (page-anchored: vertAnchor page, tblpXSpec center, tblpY 2266). Word cuts the outer row's content later than for a plain or an ordinary nested table.
- Lab nt1 (wip/lab-nt1, 90 nested rows, Arial 9, 0.5pt lines): an outer row that is NOT floating, nested table cut at the ordinary place, same as ours (R72, R75 with no lines, R58 with 3pt lines); the 450pt minimum, top alignment and the framePr change nothing.
- Lab nt1b (floating outer row, same content): Word keeps one more row than ours in every variant, and the last row stands 45pt lower than ours: bottom margin 1418: R72 at 894.7 (ours R71 at 848); margin 567: R76 (ours R75); margin 2500: R67 (ours R66). The footer distance (300/709/1200) changes nothing. The margin moves the cut one for one.
- The rule that fits all five and the real document: a nested row is kept while its top, counted WITHOUT the row lines (rows stacked at the font's line height: Arial 9 = 10.35, Noto Sans 9 = 12.26), is not below the body's foot. Lab: R72's top is 124.36 + 71 x 10.35 = 859.2 (foot 865.2: kept), R73's 869.5 (cut); margin 2500: R67 807.5 against 811.1 (kept), R68 817.8 (cut). The real document: row 44 at 329 + 43 x 12.26 = 856.2 (kept), row 45 at 868.5 (cut), the same 44 rows as Word. With the lines counted (what ours does) the page fills two rows sooner, because each row's 0.5pt line has been added to the stack by then. (Margin 567: the page's own edge, 936, caps it at R76 first.)
- Not done here: the change belongs in the parted-row cut (`cellCuts` and the `limit` in RichLayout's parted-cell code, for a page-anchored outer table), shared with the floating-table owners. Expected: fdo77887 and fdo48718-1 58.5 -> about 100. Handing it on; unclaimed.

T255 RESULT 1, tdf38575_fullWidthLine (Linux lo4, 2026-10-30): CAUSE FOUND by lab wr1 (windows, 8 variants), NOT FIXED. Word's 4 pages are caused by the HEADERS, nothing else: without the three header references (variant G) the title, the 476pt rectangle and the text sit on page 1 as ours do. With headers kept and the rectangle removed (F) the text starts right under the title on page 1 (one line less room than G). The width of the rectangle (425pt, fitting the line: same), the line spacing (same), its own paragraph (same) and rectangle alone (same) do not matter. The headers (header2 default, header3 first; header1 even) each hold a picture anchored to the header paragraph: wrapThrough bothSides, 83.85pt wide x 848pt tall (taller than the page), at x -74.85pt from the column and y -36pt from the paragraph, i.e. a black sidebar from the top of the page to its foot whose right edge is at 94pt, with distR 9pt. Word WRAPS THE BODY ROUND IT: the title's line starts at x 101.7 (the text column is 16.7pt narrower), and a line that cannot fit beside the picture (the 425/476pt rectangle) goes below the picture's foot, i.e. to the next page, where it is set at the page top anyway; the text after it starts the page after. Ours does not wrap the body round a header's or footer's picture at all (the title is at x 85, not 101.7).
- RULE TO BUILD (engine): a header's or footer's wrapped floats (square/tight/through) are exclusion bands on every page of the body, like a body float's `bands`; a line too wide for the room beside them moves below the band. Other LO documents with a wrapping float in a header or footer and low scores: lo-9181670262a2714c and lo-e643d1ee983d40a7 (a 113x57pt float at the right of the header: Word breaks the text into 5 lines, ours 3), lo-db00fd9f4baaecb1 (two wide square floats in the header), lo-95de9983615d1dbc (footer float), lo-9c6cc479ac7525b8 (59%), lo-f47abfe05a4a1d21; the 756 has 9 with such floats (all about 100% today, so their floats stay clear of the text). Not started: a few hundred lines of engine work in the page flow (`bands` in `_paginate`, seeded from the header layout's float rects at `newPage`). Unclaimed: whoever owns the engine round for text around frames / floats.

### T256 RESULT — released (Linux lo4)

Header and footer floats that the body wraps round: read, NOT built, released.

- The layout has no per-line narrowing at all. A float over body text only moves whole lines below it when less than an em is left beside it (`noRoom`). Wrapping lines beside a float needs a real line-by-line exclusion in the paragraph painter. That is a feature of its own, not a seed in `_paginate`.
- The six documents need different things: tdf38575 and lo-c6d022b6 have a full-height sidebar (a wider left margin, plus a wide object going to the next page); lo-9181670262a2714c and lo-e643d1ee983d40a7 have a 57pt picture at x 312 that narrows only the first body lines; lo-db00fd9f4baaecb1 has two page-anchored boxes; lo-95de9983615d1dbc and lo-9c6cc479ac7525b8 have footer floats low on the page. Only the sidebar pair would be helped by a margin shortcut, and tdf38575 would still need the "too wide goes below" rule.
- Build order if someone takes it: per-line exclusion in the painter for body floats first (it also serves paragraph-anchored body floats), then seed the header/footer rects (`_wrapBoxes` on the header layout's paragraphs, y = header distance + rect top, minus the body's top inset).

### Item 2 — per-run ascent/descent hook (Linux 01F2SWc8 lenovo-3): wip/lenovo3-ascent 276714692, sent to windows-1
Each run's `TextStyle` takes `ascentOverride`/`descentOverride` from its face's `baseline`/`naturalHeight` (bold/scaled variants honoured) under wordRules, where the run sits in its line (not raised, not hidden). The existing `_inkShift` is left in place and still computes its delta from the engine's (now face-true) line baseline.
Pair on the new engine (e837b7634c9), hook off vs on, Windows mode: official 756 mean 98.4 -> 98.3; LO 593 no document moves (one line count 15/15 -> 15/14, still 33.3). Official movers: zh-31d580df 99.1 -> 99.8, zh-e49d7943 99.1 -> 99.3, zh-291fcea7 99.7 -> 99.3, zh-9c5d0c3f 100 -> 99.0, zh-6d402586 96.8 -> 96.6, zh-c2c92639 98.6 -> 98.3, **zh-76700e5f 99.7 -> 65.8, zh-7773163d 97.7 -> 88.6**.
Why the two big drops: zh-76700e5f's baselines after the "5.3 制棒" heading are Word's to 0.01pt with the hook (5.3.1 267.88 vs Word 267.89, the next body line 290.70 vs 290.69), where hook-off stood 0.94pt high. The cost is the line at the foot of page 6 ("将菌棒移至层架上…", Word y -770) pushed onto page 7: the pitch down the page drifts +0.03 to +0.13pt a heading (5.3.2 +0.09 … 5.4.3 +0.34 over Word), an error hook-off hid under its 0.9 offset. That drift is not explained yet (not the hook's box: the total line height is the lineBox height both ways).
The score is nearly blind to this change by construction (3pt tolerance on a line's height): zh-0978dee9 (100) and zh-6e7ff836 (98.2), the named witnesses, do not move. So the hook is a correctness change (baselines of mixed-face lines) with no score to show for it, and a page-fit exposure on two documents.
Not landed. For windows-1: the real-face machine may not show the 0.3pt drift; if its 756 shows no drop, land. Otherwise find the +0.1 per heading first.
Also seen, unrelated: two `-k` runs of zh-0978dee9/zh-6e7ff836 on the new engine, back to back after the build, scored 2% (35 pages, hanging indent first lines 31pt in) with the hook off; the same binary, same documents, minutes later: 100/98.2, and the whole 756 hook-off 98.4. Not reproduced since; something load- or order-dependent (font registration?) is possible.
Item 2 follow-up (lenovo-3): the +0.1pt-a-heading drift in zh-76700e5f is not the hook's. Hook-off has the same line pitches (body 14.98 for Word's 15.0, headings 22.78/22.82 for 22.8/22.68), so it drifts the same way; the hook only removes the 0.94pt it stood high after the "5.3" heading, which had been hiding it.
